personality_traits: impatient and blunt, cuts to the chase ("Just pick something.")
low tolerance for indecision, treats dawdling as a personal irritant
quick to flip from flat deadpan to outsized anger, suggesting a short fuse under a composed exterior
value-conscious, reacts more strongly to the price than to the food itself
expressions: 0:00-0:03 stiff, heavy-lidded, faintly disapproving stare down at the menu while opening line is delivered
0:07 flat, mouth-closed, brow slightly lowered while saying "Just pick something" - controlled irritation, not yet angry
0:08-0:10 sharp v-shaped eyebrows, glaring wide eyes, mouth thrown open in a shout as the price ($29) reaction plays in extreme close-up - full anger/outrage
gestures: sits rigid and upright behind an open menu held with both hands
index finger jabs/points down at a specific line in the menu while speaking, an emphatic 'look at this' gesture
head and torso pulled taut into frame for the angry close-up, no shrinking or softening of posture
characters.interactions_notes: Faces the woman across a small two-top table but keeps his gaze mostly on the menu rather than on her, underscoring that his frustration is about time/decision-making rather than direct conflict with her. He opens the exchange and delivers the shortest, most direct lines, positioning him as the one trying to move the interaction along; his anger at the end is the payoff/punchline reaction shot, flipping the power dynamic from 'patient nudger' to the more visibly rattled of the two.

personality_traits: indecisive in the moment but articulate about why once pressed
dry, dismissive wit - deflates hype with a flat one-liner ("a mushroom that got famous")
frugal/principled about value, unbothered by being called out for stalling
self-possessed; delivers her final line without defensiveness, more matter-of-fact than embarrassed
expressions: 0:02-0:04 droopy, heavy-lidded eyes and slightly parted mouth reading as a mid-sigh, tired look aimed down at the menu (matches on-screen word 'SIGHING')
0:04-0:06 narrowed eyes, small downturned frown while stating 'Everything has truffle on it' - dry, unimpressed delivery
0:07-0:08 raised brows and slightly parted mouth, a beat of hesitation/consideration (on-screen word 'SOMETHING') as she processes being told to just pick
0:08-0:10 relaxed, half-lidded, faintly smug/settled expression as she lands the punchline about the mushroom being 'famous' - no strain, delivered as an obvious conclusion
gestures: holds the menu upright with both hands close to her body, more guarded posture than the man's
closes the menu and rests both hands flat on top of it once she has landed on her reasoning, a small physical full-stop punctuating her line
minimal head movement; stays composed and still even as the man's reaction escalates beside her
characters.interactions_notes: Seated opposite the husband at the same small table, she rarely meets his eyes directly, instead looking at the menu or into middle distance - the couple trades lines in a clean back-and-forth without overlapping speech, typical of a scripted sitcom-style call-and-response. She holds conversational ground calmly against his mounting impatience, and her closing line is what appears to trigger his angry close-up reaction, making her the one who (unintentionally) escalates the scene despite being the calmer, more deadpan of the two.
